desc: Check whether a website is configured with X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors to defend against clickjacking attacks
meta.description: Check whether a website is configured with X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors to defend against clickjacking attacks
meta.title: Clickjacking Test - S-Jiffy
ui.12: The target site should add the header
ui.14: to prevent the page from being embedded by third-party sites.
ui.2: How it works and its limits:
ui.21: The target refuses to render in an iframe; embedding is blocked by X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors
ui.22: This site has anti-clickjacking protection, restricting its pages from being embedded by third-party sites via response headers. Clickjacking risk is low.
ui.24: The target returned an error; it may have refused the connection
ui.25: The target returned an error response; it may have refused the connection or be temporarily unavailable. Verify the URL and reachability before retrying; some browsers also fail to load when embedding is blocked.
ui.27: No target response received within 3.5 seconds
ui.28: The target did not respond within 3.5 seconds; the network may be unreachable, the response slow, or the request blocked. As a pure front-end tool it cannot distinguish these cases; verify reachability and retry.
ui.32: Cannot read response headers cross-origin; verdict based on iframe probe
ui.4: The target page rendered successfully inside an iframe and can be embedded
ui.5: Cross-origin load succeeded; the target page can be embedded (recommend confirming with response headers)
ui.7: 1. This is a pure front-end check; results are affected by browser policy differences and target-site reachability, for reference only.
ui.8: 2. When the target blocks embedding via X-Frame-Options or CSP, browsers behave differently (some load successfully but with unreadable content, some fail to load), which may skew the verdict.
ui.9: 3. The result represents the "current browser perspective"; we recommend confirming with response-header info or server-side tools.
